text: Muskmelon vines are trained up a stake-and-net trellis roughly 1.8-2 m tall built from bamboo poles and twine/net. As vines grow, side shoots are pinched and only the main stem plus a small number of fruit-bearing laterals are retained; each plant is typically limited to a small number of developing fruits so the plant's energy concentrates into fewer, larger, better-quality melons. Developing fruit is sometimes cradled in a mesh or plastic sling hung from the trellis to keep it off the ground and reduce rot and pest damage.
